data.title: Tilray Stockholders Reelect Directors at Annual Meeting

data.title: Patrick Industries Shareholders Approve LCI Industries Merger Proposals
data.description:
Patrick Industries ( (PATK) ) just unveiled an update.

On November 18, 2026, Patrick Industries shareholders approved four proposals related to the company’s all-stock merger with LCI Industries, including issuing Patrick shares to LCI stockholders, increasing authorized common stock, amending the articles of incorporation and permitting potential adjournments. At least 97% of votes cast, representing approximately 93% of Patrick’s outstanding shares, supported the proposals, while approximately 98% of LCI votes cast, representing approximately 82% of its outstanding shares, supported the necessary merger proposal.

Patrick and LCI said they had received the shareholder approvals required to complete the merger. The transaction remained subject to required regulatory approvals and other customary closing conditions.

data.title: Duos Technologies Updates Investors on Data Center Growth
data.description:
Duos Technologies Group ( (DUOT) ) has issued an announcement.

On November 18, 2026, Duos Technologies Group posted an updated investor presentation. The presentation described approximately $560 million in signed colocation value, including a 10-year, 20-megawatt agreement worth more than $400 million, with a weighted average lease term of about seven years.

At the Columbus campus acquired in 2026, Nistar signed a master services agreement for up to 2 megawatts on July 7, while a five-year, 10-megawatt hyperscaler agreement worth more than $111 million was announced on July 16. By October 2026, an initial deployment serving a hyperscale anchor customer was in service on a cluster of 2,304 NVIDIA B300 GPUs.

On September 30, 2026, the GPU fleet special-purpose vehicle was sold to Axe Compute, which repaid approximately $87.8 million of its debt, while the customer continued under a revised five-year agreement. The presentation also cited positive adjusted EBITDA for continuing operations in the third quarter of 2026 and identified more than 100 megawatts of opportunities under evaluation in 5- to 10-megawatt tranches, with no commitments assumed.

data.title: MEDIROM Files Annual Report and Appeals Nasdaq Delisting Determination
data.description:
MEDIROM Healthcare Technologies ( (MRM) ) just unveiled an update.

On November 13, 2026, MEDIROM Healthcare Technologies received a Nasdaq notice after failing to file its 2025 Annual Report within a previously granted extension, leaving it out of compliance with Nasdaq’s periodic-reporting requirement. The notice stated that, absent an appeal, trading in the company’s American Depositary Shares would be suspended and delisted at the opening of business on November 24, 2026.

On November 18, 2026, MEDIROM filed the Annual Report and submitted a hearing request to appeal the determination, automatically staying any suspension for 15 days from that date while the company also requested an extended stay. The filing was presented in support of continued listing, but it did not resolve a separate minimum bid-price deficiency for which Nasdaq had granted the company until April 5, 2027 to regain compliance.

data.title: Tronox Reassures Investors on Liquidity Amid Creditor Reports
data.description:
TRONOX ( (TROX) ) has provided an announcement.

On November 18, 2026, Tronox responded to a November 17 Wall Street Journal article reporting that two groups of its creditors had engaged law firms labeled “restructuring advisors”; the company said it had never engaged with either group or its advisors. The company said the engagements were formed last year; the article said one was recently reinstated, but Tronox said neither development signaled imminent or likely negotiations.

Tronox reported $509 million of liquidity at September 30, 2026, comprising $136 million in cash and cash equivalents and $373 million available under revolving credit agreements, and said its next significant debt maturity was not until 2029. The company said it had no financial covenants on term loans or bonds and that its chief executive was confident it had ample liquidity to operate and remain current on obligations.

data.title: Vodafone Reports H1 FY27 Revenue Growth and €3.6 Billion Loss
data.description:
Vodafone ( (VOD) ) just unveiled an update.

Vodafone Group Plc, a provider of mobile and fixed connectivity, financial services and digital solutions across European and African markets, reported H1 FY27 results on November 18, 2026. Total revenue rose 11.4% to €21.9 billion and service revenue increased 12.8% to €18.4 billion, including 5.8% organic growth, with consolidation of Safaricom, VodafoneThree and Telekom Romania contributing to total revenue.

Vodafone reported a €3.6 billion loss for the period, compared with a €1.1 billion profit in H1 FY26, citing non-cash charges including a Germany impairment and a UK deferred-tax-asset write-down; these were partly offset by a non-cash gain from the Safaricom transaction. The interim dividend rose 2.5% to 2.306 eurocents per share, while H1 gross opex savings reached €0.2 billion and about 3,000 role reductions were delivered in Europe and shared operations.

data.description:
